newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says receives business proposal from BT, MCI.
newsitem.headline: NTT says receives business proposal from BT, MCI.

text.p: Top officials from British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp visited Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp earlier this week and made a proposal on international business, an NTT spokesman said on Thursday.

He said NTT president Junichiro Miyazu met visiting BT chairman Sir Iain Vallance and MCI chairman Bert Roberts earlier this week to discuss business, but refused to comment on details of the proposal.
BT, along with most of its global telecoms rivals, has long sought to link up with the Japanese phone giant and gain a foothold in lucrative Asian markets.

NTT, which only last month won regulatory approval to offer international services as part of a broad restructuring, said earlier this month that it hoped to pursue an independent approach to gaining customers in the global market, rather than seeking tie-ups with international rivals.
The company, the world's biggest telecoms firm, currently has a near-monopoly in Japan's domestic telecoms market.

"We understand that the two firms made some kind of proposal on international business, but haven't heard the details," the NTT spokesman said, adding that NTT has received many such requests from large communications operators around the world.

The proposal made by BT and MCI of the United States, which are seeking to merge later this year in a major international telecoms alliance, is being studied at NTT's international business division, he said.

NTT did not confirm whether president Miyazu would meet BT President and Chief Executive Peter Bonfield later this month when he visits Japan to attend a Japan-Britain conference of business leaders, politicians and academics.
Although NTT executives have said the company will adopt a go-it-alone stance in the international market, president Miyazu has signalled that the position may be a open to change.
"Many firms are seeking tie-ups with NTT, but they of course would change their strategy if the situation changes. We also should be flexible," Miyazu recently told a media reception.
Some analysts believe NTT's emphasis on an independent approach may be a negotiating ploy to improve its position with regard to potential partners.
